text.p: Southern Co expects "some early-on, slight earnings dilution," from its acquisition of Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd, chief executive A.W. Dahlberg told security analysts Wednesday.
The dilution will not be enough to affect the payout ratio, he told a teleconference.
Chief Financial Officer Larry Westbrook said the "maximum dilution" would reduce earnings "as much as a couple of cents" per share in 1997.
In 1998, he continued, it will "add about a nickel to that. As much as $0.07" per share.
In 1999, he told the analysts, the acquisition will become accretive, adding as much as $0.02 per share.
And he pointed out that a month or two of hot summer weather would more than offset any dilution seen.
Dahlberg also told the analysts Southern expects its growing power marketing organization to be "in the top 10 (such companies) by the end of the year."

He said the company is looking to independent power plants, power marketing and industrial energy management for growth in North America, noting that Southern's core utility business is "growing at a slow pace."
